newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Colonial says Alltel deal to cut costs.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Colonial says Alltel deal to cut costs.

text.p: Life insurance and banking group Colonial Ltd said on Thursday that a A$532 million deal to outsource information technology would lower its costs to income ratio, improve customer service and boost flexibility.

Colonial managing director Stuart James said the agreement with U.S. based Alltel Information Services would significantly reduce information technology costs for Colonial State Bank. The seven-year deal includes re-engineering and operation of an updated banking information system for about the same amount as the bank would have paid in operating costs, James said.
"It will lower the bank's costs to income ratio...and it will provide us with a better level of customer service," James told a news conference.
The deal would also give the bank the flexibility to eventually offer customers a wider range of financial services, he said.
The agreement would take effect from May 1997 and changes should be in place by June 1999.
Colonial, a mutual which plans to float on the stock exchange later this year, said the agreement only covered the Colonial State Bank.
However, James said it could be extended to Colonial's life office operations if successful.
Alltel Information Services, a unit of Alltel Corp, said the deal with Colonia was significantl for the company, which currently has two other, smaller contracts in Australia.
Alltel said its agreement was worth A$435 million, which excluded agreements by Colonial with subcontractors.
